program.name: Doctoral-Track Major in Finance, Economics & Quantitative Markets

tiers.name: Foundations
tiers.standard: Rigorous first-two-years university mathematics, computing, statistics and economics.

tiers.name: Major
tiers.standard: Complete undergraduate finance major at a top program, plus the quantitative depth most majors skip.

tiers.name: Master's
tiers.standard: MFE / MSF / MSc Economics level: continuous-time finance, econometrics, and production research.

tiers.name: Doctoral
tiers.standard: First-year PhD coursework in asset pricing, econometrics and macro, then original research.

milestones.name: Major Complete
milestones.rule: Every F and U module project passed, plus every studio of tier F or U.

milestones.name: Master's-Equivalent
milestones.rule: MAJOR, plus every M module project and every M studio.

milestones.name: Doctoral Candidate
milestones.rule: MASTERS, plus every D module and studio, including the CAP3 qualifying exam.

milestones.name: Doctoral
milestones.rule: CANDIDATE, plus the CAP4 thesis defended against the rubric.

tracks.name: Corporate Finance / Investment Banking / Private Equity
Research doctorate (minimum prerequisite path to thesis)

atlas.title: Repository skeleton
atlas.delivers: Typed Python package, CLI entry point, test harness, pre-commit, CI config.

atlas.title: Data layer
atlas.delivers: DuckDB store, point-in-time schema, ingestion for FRED / French / Shiller / Treasury / EDGAR, data manifest with hashes.

atlas.title: Data-quality and EDA reports
atlas.delivers: Automated profiling (gaps, outliers, stale prints, splits) on any Atlas dataset.

atlas.title: Time-series toolkit
atlas.delivers: ARMA, GARCH, HAR and Kalman estimators with forecast-evaluation tests.

atlas.title: Curve engine
atlas.delivers: Bootstrapping plus Nelson–Siegel and Svensson fitting, with day-count conventions.

atlas.title: Pricing library
atlas.delivers: BSM, binomial, finite differences, Monte Carlo and LSMC with Greeks; C++ kernel behind a Python API.

atlas.title: Cross-sectional engine
atlas.delivers: Portfolio sorts, Fama–MacBeth with Shanken correction, GRS test.

atlas.title: Research-integrity module
atlas.delivers: Deflated Sharpe, PBO, Romano–Wolf and BH adjustments, applied automatically to every backtest.

atlas.title: Backtester
atlas.delivers: Event-driven engine with signal/execution lags, cost hooks, walk-forward and purged CV.

atlas.title: Execution and cost models
atlas.delivers: Square-root impact, Almgren–Chriss scheduler, implementation-shortfall accounting.

atlas.title: Portfolio construction
atlas.delivers: Shrinkage covariance, MV / risk-parity / vol-target allocators with constraint handling.

atlas.title: Risk engine
atlas.delivers: VaR / ES (historical, parametric, EVT), VaR backtests, scenario and stress engine.

atlas.title: Term-premium and rates-RV module
atlas.delivers: Affine-model term premium, carry and roll-down, curve-trade P&L attribution.

atlas.title: Credit module
atlas.delivers: Merton / Black–Cox / reduced-form pricers, distance to default, spread decomposition.

atlas.title: Fundamentals engine
atlas.delivers: EDGAR XBRL ingestion, standardized statements, ratio and accrual-quality library.

atlas.title: Valuation engine
atlas.delivers: DCF, residual income and multiples, with scenario and sensitivity grids driven by A15.

atlas.title: ML pipeline
atlas.delivers: Feature store, purged/embargoed CV, model registry, SHAP reports, plugged into A8 and A9.

atlas.title: Nowcasting and regime dashboard
atlas.delivers: Real-time-vintage dynamic factor nowcast, regime classifier, cross-asset monitor.

atlas.title: Systemic-risk monitor
atlas.delivers: CoVaR, SRISK and MES on open data, with alert thresholds.

atlas.title: Macro trade-construction engine
atlas.delivers: View → expression → sizing → scenario P&L, reusing A5, A6, A11, A12.

tracks.name: Corporate Finance / Investment Banking / Private Equity
Research doctorate (minimum prerequisite path to thesis)

modules.title: How to Study This Program
modules.core: Evidence grades (T/A/B/C/D/X); how to read a paper (question, identification, data, inference, robustness); steelmanning; the project ladder; how Atlas compounds; the notation conventions.
sources: Dunlosky et al. (2013), Psychological Science in the Public Interest 14(1)
Keshav (2007), 'How to Read a Paper', ACM SIGCOMM CCR 37(3)
modules.lab: Navigate the prerequisite DAG; run a first Pyodide cell.

project.title: Paper teardown
project.brief: Take one assigned classic paper and produce a one-page structured teardown: question, mechanism, data, identification, main result with its locator, the weakest assumption, and the evidence grade it deserves.
project.deliverable: One-page teardown in the in-page template.

modules.title: Diagnostics, Mastery Gating & Spaced Retrieval
modules.core: How placement tests let you skip what you already know; mastery thresholds; the spaced-retrieval scheduler; interleaved review; why rereading is a weak strategy and retrieval is a strong one.
sources: Kalyuga, Ayres, Chandler & Sweller (2003), Educational Psychologist 38(1)
modules.lab: Take the program-wide placement diagnostic; the result unlocks test-out paths.

project.title: Personal study plan
project.brief: From your placement results and the track hour totals, build a dated study plan covering weekly hours, track choice, review cadence and milestones.
project.deliverable: Exported plan JSON plus a half-page rationale.

studio.title: Numerical Mathematics Library
studio.brief: Implement from scratch a root finder (Brent), a QP solver (active-set) and a Monte Carlo engine with antithetic and control variates. Verify each against SciPy to stated tolerances, and include a written proof of convergence for the root finder.

modules.title: Precalculus & Mathematical Reasoning
modules.core: Algebra, functions, exponentials and logarithms (continuous compounding), sequences and series (annuities, perpetuities), sets, quantifiers, direct proof, contradiction, induction.
sources: Velleman, How to Prove It, 3rd ed. (2019)

project.title: Annuity and mortgage engine
project.brief: Derive the closed forms for annuity, perpetuity and growing-perpetuity values by induction and geometric series, then implement and test them, including a full amortization schedule.
project.deliverable: Proofs and a tested Python module.

modules.title: Single & Multivariable Calculus
modules.core: Limits, derivatives, Taylor's theorem, integration, partial derivatives, gradients, Jacobians, Hessians, multiple integrals, implicit-function and envelope theorems.
sources: Hubbard & Hubbard, Vector Calculus, Linear Algebra, and Differential Forms, 5th ed. (2015)
modules.lab: Taylor expansion of a bond price: duration and convexity preview.

project.title: Sensitivity engine
project.brief: Build first- and second-order sensitivities for any differentiable pricing function, using analytic, finite-difference and automatic-differentiation approaches, and characterize where finite differences break.
project.deliverable: Tested module plus an error-analysis note.

modules.title: Linear Algebra
modules.core: Vector spaces, linear maps, eigendecomposition, spectral theorem, SVD, positive-semidefinite matrices, projections, least-squares geometry, PCA.
sources: Axler, Linear Algebra Done Right, 4th ed. (2024)
Strang, Introduction to Linear Algebra, 6th ed. (2023)
modules.lab: PCA of the U.S. Treasury curve (embedded data): level, slope, curvature.

project.title: Covariance-matrix doctor
project.brief: Diagnose and repair non-PSD empirical correlation matrices (nearest-correlation projection, eigenvalue clipping). Compare the effect of each repair on downstream portfolio weights.
project.deliverable: Tested module plus a comparison report.

modules.title: Probability
modules.core: Distributions, expectation, MGFs and characteristic functions, the multivariate normal, conditioning, LLN, CLT, heavy tails, and the failure of the CLT under infinite variance.
sources: Blitzstein & Hwang, Introduction to Probability, 2nd ed. (2019)
modules.lab: Sample-mean behaviour under Gaussian, Student-t(3) and Cauchy draws.

project.title: Tail-risk simulator
project.brief: Simulate portfolio losses under multivariate Gaussian vs. multivariate Student-t returns with matched covariance. Quantify how the 99% loss estimate changes, and prove the moment conditions behind the result.

modules.title: Real Analysis
modules.core: Completeness of R, sequences and series, continuity, uniform convergence, compactness, metric spaces, fixed-point theorems (Banach), Riemann–Stieltjes.
sources: Rudin, Principles of Mathematical Analysis, 3rd ed. (1976)
modules.lab: Banach fixed-point iteration solving a Bellman equation.

project.title: Contraction-mapping solver
project.brief: Prove the Bellman operator for a discounted savings problem is a contraction, then implement value-function iteration with a certified error bound.

modules.title: Measure-Theoretic Probability
modules.core: Sigma-algebras, Lebesgue integral, MCT and DCT, Fubini, Radon–Nikodym, conditional expectation as L2 projection, filtrations, discrete-time martingales, optional stopping, martingale convergence.
sources: Billingsley, Probability and Measure, anniversary ed. (2012)
modules.lab: Martingale betting-system simulator: why doubling strategies fail under finite capital.

project.title: Proof portfolio: martingales
project.brief: Write complete proofs of optional stopping (bounded case), Doob's maximal inequality, and the martingale convergence theorem, then verify each numerically on simulated paths.

modules.title: Optimization
modules.core: Convex sets and functions, Lagrange multipliers, KKT conditions, duality, quadratic programming, dynamic programming and the Bellman equation.
sources: Stokey & Lucas, Recursive Methods in Economic Dynamics (1989)
modules.lab: Efficient frontier via QP with and without a short-sale constraint.

project.title: Constrained allocator
project.brief: Build a mean-variance allocator supporting box, turnover and sector constraints. Verify the KKT conditions hold at every returned solution.

modules.title: Numerical Methods & Scientific Computing
modules.core: IEEE 754, conditioning and stability, root finding, linear solvers, interpolation, quadrature, finite differences, random-number generation, Monte Carlo and variance reduction.
sources: Goldberg (1991), 'What Every Computer Scientist Should Know About Floating-Point Arithmetic', ACM Computing Surveys 23(1)
Glasserman, Monte Carlo Methods in Financial Engineering (2003)
modules.lab: Catastrophic cancellation; antithetic and control-variate efficiency.

project.title: Robust implied-volatility solver
project.brief: Build an implied-vol solver that never fails on valid inputs (deep ITM/OTM, near expiry), using bracketing with Newton acceleration. Stress it on a generated grid of a million inputs.
project.deliverable: Tested solver plus a failure-region report.

studio.title: Limit Order Book Matching Engine
studio.brief: Build a price-time-priority matching engine (limit, market, cancel, modify) in C++ with Python bindings. Include deterministic replay of a message log, property-based tests, and latency benchmarks. MS2 and MS3 reuse it.

modules.title: Programming in Python from Zero
modules.core: Types, control flow, functions, data structures, classes and protocols, type hints, errors, files, modules, NumPy and pandas fundamentals.
modules.lab: Vectorized returns computation vs. loops: correctness and speed.

project.title: Atlas A1: repository skeleton
project.brief: Create the Atlas package with typed modules, a CLI, a pytest suite, formatting and linting config, and CI. Every later Atlas milestone builds on this repository.

modules.title: Algorithms & Data Structures
modules.core: Complexity, arrays, hash maps, heaps, trees, graphs, sorting, searching, dynamic programming, and the data structures behind order books and event queues.
sources: Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest & Stein, Introduction to Algorithms, 4th ed. (2022)
modules.lab: Heap-based event queue vs. a sorted list at scale.

project.title: Streaming statistics library
project.brief: Implement O(1)-update rolling mean, variance (Welford), min/max (monotonic deque) and an approximate quantile sketch. Prove the correctness of Welford's update.

modules.title: Data, Databases & SQL
modules.core: The relational model, SQL, joins, window functions, ASOF joins, indexing, columnar storage, Parquet, DuckDB.
modules.lab: ASOF JOIN of trades to quotes in DuckDB-WASM.

project.title: Atlas A2: data layer
project.brief: Build the Atlas data layer: a DuckDB store with a point-in-time schema, ingestion for FRED, French, Shiller, Treasury and EDGAR, and a manifest with source, licence, retrieval time and hash.

modules.title: Software Engineering & Reproducible Research
modules.core: Git workflows, testing (unit, property-based, regression), typing, packaging, CI, environment pinning, determinism, code review.
sources: Wilson et al. (2014), 'Best Practices for Scientific Computing', PLOS Biology 12(1)
Wilson et al. (2017), 'Good Enough Practices in Scientific Computing', PLOS Computational Biology 13(6)
modules.lab: A property-based test finds a bug a unit test missed.

project.title: Reproducibility audit
project.brief: Take a deliberately broken research repository (unpinned, non-deterministic, no tests) and make it reproduce bit-for-bit, documenting every fix.
project.deliverable: Fixed repository plus an audit log.

modules.title: C++ & Systems for Finance
modules.core: Modern C++ (C++20): value semantics, RAII, templates, the STL, memory hierarchy, cache effects, compilation, Python bindings, WASM compilation.
sources: Stroustrup, A Tour of C++, 3rd ed. (2022)
Drepper (2007), 'What Every Programmer Should Know About Memory'

project.title: C++ Monte Carlo kernel
project.brief: Port a Python Monte Carlo pricer to C++ with identical seeded output, expose it to Python, and document the speedup and where it comes from.
project.deliverable: C++ kernel, bindings, equivalence tests, benchmark.

modules.title: Parallel & High-Performance Computing
modules.core: Amdahl's law, threads vs. processes, SIMD, GPU programming model, parallel RNG streams, profiling, latency vs. throughput engineering.
sources: Hennessy & Patterson, Computer Architecture: A Quantitative Approach, 6th ed. (2017)
modules.lab: Parallel Monte Carlo with independent RNG streams: reproducibility check.

project.title: Parallel risk run
project.brief: Parallelize a full-portfolio Monte Carlo VaR with reproducible RNG streams, achieving a measured speedup and reconciling the result to the serial run.

studio.title: Predictive-Regression Stress Test
studio.brief: Replicate the CAPE / dividend-yield return-predictability evidence on embedded Shiller data. Apply Stambaugh bias correction, HAC inference, out-of-sample R-squared, and multiple-testing adjustment across predictors. Write the referee-grade verdict.

modules.title: Exploratory Data Analysis & Visualization
modules.core: Distributions, robust summaries, outliers, missing data, stale prices and splits, graphical perception, how charts mislead.
modules.lab: Anscombe's quartet; spotting a split-adjustment error.

project.title: Atlas A3: data-quality reports
project.brief: Add automated profiling to Atlas, flagging gaps, outliers, stale prints and corporate-action breaks on any dataset in the store.

modules.title: Statistical Inference
modules.core: Estimators, bias and variance, MLE and its asymptotics, Fisher information, Cramér–Rao, hypothesis tests, power, confidence intervals, Bayesian inference, the bootstrap.
modules.lab: Bootstrap vs. asymptotic confidence intervals for a Sharpe ratio.

project.title: Power analysis for a strategy
project.brief: Compute how many years of data are needed to detect a given Sharpe ratio at a given power, analytically and by simulation, and reconcile the two.
project.deliverable: Analysis notebook plus a one-page memo.

modules.title: Linear Regression
modules.core: OLS geometry, Gauss–Markov, asymptotics, heteroskedasticity-robust and HAC errors, clustering, errors-in-variables, Stambaugh bias in predictive regressions.

project.title: Inference engine
project.brief: Implement OLS with classical, White, Newey–West and two-way clustered standard errors, validated against statsmodels and by simulated coverage rates.
project.deliverable: Tested module plus a coverage study.

modules.title: Time Series
modules.core: Stationarity, ARMA, Wold, unit roots, spurious regression, cointegration, VARs and identification, state space and the Kalman filter, Markov switching.

project.title: Pairs-trading audit
project.brief: Test claimed cointegrated pairs on open data with correct critical values, measure half-life stability out of sample, and show how many pairs survive.

modules.title: Volatility Econometrics
modules.core: ARCH, GARCH, EGARCH, realized volatility, HAR, forecast evaluation (QLIKE, MSE).

project.title: Atlas A4: time-series toolkit
project.brief: Add ARMA, GARCH, HAR and Kalman estimators to Atlas, with robust loss-function-based forecast evaluation.

modules.title: GMM & Cross-Sectional Econometrics
modules.core: GMM theory and efficient weighting, Fama–MacBeth, Shanken correction, the GRS test, panel fixed effects.

project.title: Two-pass estimator with errors-in-variables correction
project.brief: Implement Fama–MacBeth with Shanken-corrected standard errors and GMM equivalents, and show when the correction changes the conclusion.
project.deliverable: Tested module plus a replication note.

modules.title: Causal Inference & Event Studies
modules.core: Potential outcomes, IV and weak instruments, difference-in-differences (including staggered adoption), RDD, event studies, synthetic control.
modules.lab: Event study with correct abnormal-return variance.

project.title: Policy-shock event study
project.brief: Measure asset-price reactions to a set of scheduled macro announcements using open data, with clustering-robust inference and placebo dates.

modules.title: Research Integrity & Multiple Testing
modules.core: Data snooping, the Reality Check, SPA, Romano–Wolf, FDR, the factor-zoo t-stat hurdle, the deflated Sharpe ratio, probability of backtest overfitting, p-hacking.
sources: Bailey, Borwein, López de Prado & Zhu (2017), Journal of Computational Finance 20(4)
modules.lab: Random-strategy overfitting engine: in-sample vs. out-of-sample Sharpe.

project.title: Atlas A8: research-integrity module
project.brief: Add deflated Sharpe, PBO, Romano–Wolf and BH adjustments to Atlas, applied automatically to every backtest result object.

studio.title: Central Bank Simulator
studio.brief: Estimate a Taylor rule on FRED data, solve and calibrate the three-equation New Keynesian model, and run policy counterfactuals (ZLB, forward guidance, supply shock). Defend the policy recommendation in a two-page memo.

modules.title: Microeconomics
modules.core: Consumer and producer theory, demand and supply, elasticity, market structures, welfare, externalities, public goods.
modules.lab: Comparative statics of a market equilibrium.

project.title: Market-structure lab
project.brief: Model an exchange-fee market under monopoly vs. Cournot vs. Bertrand competition, and quantify the welfare and fee outcomes.

modules.title: Game Theory & Information Economics
modules.core: Nash and Bayesian-Nash equilibrium, adverse selection, signaling, screening, moral hazard, mechanism design, auctions.
modules.lab: Winner's curse in a common-value auction.

project.title: Treasury auction design
project.brief: Simulate uniform-price vs. discriminatory auctions with strategic bidders and compare revenue, bid shading and allocative efficiency.

modules.title: Decision Theory Under Risk & Ambiguity
modules.core: Expected utility, Arrow–Pratt risk aversion, stochastic dominance, Epstein–Zin recursive preferences, prospect theory, ambiguity aversion.
sources: Gilboa & Schmeidler (1989), Journal of Mathematical Economics 18(2)
modules.lab: Certainty equivalents of one gamble under four preference models.

project.title: Preference elicitation
project.brief: Design and run an in-page lottery questionnaire, estimate the participant's risk-aversion and loss-aversion parameters by MLE, and report the uncertainty.

modules.title: General Equilibrium & Information in Markets
modules.core: Arrow–Debreu, complete vs. incomplete markets, rational expectations, the Grossman–Stiglitz paradox, the no-trade theorem.
modules.lab: Grossman–Stiglitz equilibrium: fraction informed vs. information cost.

project.title: Price-informativeness model
project.brief: Solve a noisy rational-expectations model numerically, and show how price informativeness responds to noise-trader volume and information cost.

modules.title: Macroeconomics I: Aggregates, Cycles & Policy
modules.core: National accounts, growth accounting, the Solow model, IS-LM and AD-AS, the Phillips curve and the natural rate, central banking and fiscal policy basics.
modules.lab: Growth accounting on embedded national-accounts data.

project.title: Macro dashboard v0
project.brief: Assemble GDP, inflation, unemployment, policy-rate and term-spread series from Atlas into a documented dashboard, with a one-page cycle diagnosis.

modules.title: Macroeconomics II: Dynamic General Equilibrium
modules.core: RBC, New Keynesian models, determinacy, heterogeneous-agent (HANK) models, solution and estimation methods.
sources: Galí, Monetary Policy, Inflation, and the Business Cycle, 2nd ed. (2015)

project.title: NK model solver
project.brief: Solve the NK model by undetermined coefficients and numerically, verify the determinacy (Taylor) principle, and reproduce the canonical impulse responses.
project.deliverable: Tested solver plus a figure set.

modules.title: Monetary Economics & Central Banking
modules.core: Policy rules, time inconsistency, the ZLB, operating frameworks (floor vs. corridor), QE channels and evidence, shock identification, r-star, the fiscal theory of the price level, the 2021–23 inflation.
sources: Gagnon, Raskin, Remache & Sack (2011), International Journal of Central Banking 7(1)
Krishnamurthy & Vissing-Jorgensen (2011), Brookings Papers on Economic Activity
Holston, Laubach & Williams (2017), Journal of International Economics 108
Cochrane, The Fiscal Theory of the Price Level (2023)
modules.lab: Taylor-rule prescriptions vs. the realized policy rate.

project.title: Monetary-shock identification
project.brief: Construct high-frequency policy surprises from embedded futures-implied rates, estimate their effects with local projections, and compare the result with the Romer–Romer narrative series.

modules.debate: Does QE work mainly through portfolio balance or through signalling?

modules.title: International Macro & the Dollar
modules.core: Balance of payments, UIP failure, CIP deviations, the trilemma, Mundell–Fleming, Dornbusch overshooting, the dominant-currency paradigm, the global financial cycle, safe assets and convenience yields.
sources: Rey (2013), Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium
Obstfeld & Rogoff, Foundations of International Macroeconomics (1996)
modules.lab: Fama UIP regression on embedded FX and rate data.

project.title: CIP-basis monitor
project.brief: Compute cross-currency bases from public rates and FX data, relate them to quarter-ends and dollar-funding stress, and explain the mechanism.

modules.debate: Is UIP failure a risk premium or mispricing?

modules.title: Sovereign Debt, Crises & Political Economy
modules.core: Debt dynamics and r minus g, sovereign default, currency-crisis models, sudden stops, banking crises, the Reinhart–Rogoff replication episode.
sources: Krugman (1979), Journal of Money, Credit and Banking 11(3)
Reinhart & Rogoff, This Time Is Different (2009)
Herndon, Ash & Pollin (2014), Cambridge Journal of Economics 38(2)
modules.lab: Debt-dynamics simulator under stochastic r and g.

project.title: Sovereign risk report
project.brief: Build a debt-sustainability analysis for one country from public data, with fan charts and a default-probability mapping, and defend it in a two-page memo.

studio.title: Market Structure Field Guide
studio.brief: For one asset class, produce a complete field guide covering venues, participants, instruments, order types, clearing and settlement, typical costs, and the three biggest structural risks, every claim sourced.

modules.title: The Financial System, Markets & Instruments
modules.core: Money and credit creation, intermediaries, exchanges vs. OTC, instrument taxonomy across equities, rates, credit, FX, commodities and derivatives, order types, clearing and settlement.
sources: Mishkin, The Economics of Money, Banking and Financial Markets, 13th ed. (2022)
McLeay, Radia & Thomas (2014), Bank of England Quarterly Bulletin Q1
modules.lab: Trace one trade from order entry to settlement.

project.title: Instrument cash-flow engine
project.brief: Represent bonds, futures, swaps and options as dated cash-flow or payoff objects with a common interface, and test each against hand-computed examples.

modules.title: Derivatives Fundamentals
modules.core: Forwards, futures, swaps, option payoffs, no-arbitrage forward pricing, put–call parity, one-period and multi-period binomial pricing, using the Black–Scholes formula.
sources: Hull, Options, Futures, and Other Derivatives, 11th ed. (2021)

project.title: Arbitrage scanner
project.brief: Given an embedded option-chain snapshot, detect put–call parity and convexity violations net of a stated cost model, and explain each one found.

modules.title: Market Efficiency: The Evidence Primer
modules.core: The efficient-markets hypothesis and its forms, the arithmetic of active management, luck vs. skill, the anomalies preview, behavioral explanations.
modules.lab: Sharpe's arithmetic of active management, simulated.

project.title: Fund-skill test
project.brief: Using a simulated fund universe with known skill, show how many funds look skilled by chance, and recover the true skilled set with a bootstrap.

modules.debate: Are markets efficient? (primer; full debate in AP8 and CAP2)

studio.title: Forensic Audit of a Public Company
studio.brief: Using SEC EDGAR filings and XBRL data for a real issuer over five or more years, produce a forensic report covering accrual quality, revenue-recognition changes, cash-conversion trends and M-score / F-score, with each red flag tied to the filing line it comes from.

modules.title: Financial Accounting
modules.core: Double-entry bookkeeping, accrual accounting, the three statements and how they link, GAAP vs. IFRS, revenue recognition (ASC 606 / IFRS 15), leases (ASC 842 / IFRS 16), stock compensation, deferred taxes.
modules.lab: Build linked three statements from a transaction ledger.

project.title: Three-statement model from raw transactions
project.brief: Post 200 generated transactions, produce balance sheet, income statement and cash-flow statement, and prove the statements articulate.

modules.title: Financial Statement Analysis & Earnings Quality
modules.core: Ratio analysis, DuPont decomposition, cash-flow quality, the accruals anomaly, earnings management, the F-score and M-score.
sources: Penman, Financial Statement Analysis and Security Valuation, 5th ed. (2013)
Dechow, Sloan & Sweeney (1995), The Accounting Review 70(2)

project.title: Atlas A15: fundamentals engine
project.brief: Ingest EDGAR XBRL into Atlas, standardize the statements across filers, and implement the ratio, accrual and score library.

modules.title: Earnings, Disclosure & Market Reaction
modules.core: Information content of earnings, post-earnings-announcement drift, disclosure and guidance, the residual-income link between accounting and value.
sources: Ball & Brown (1968), Journal of Accounting Research 6(2)
Bernard & Thomas (1989), Journal of Accounting Research 27 (Supplement)

project.title: PEAD replication
project.brief: Replicate post-earnings-announcement drift with the student's own price data (bring-your-own-data mode) and Atlas fundamentals. Report the post-2000 decay and net-of-cost results.

studio.title: The Full Deal
studio.brief: For one public company: a full DCF and multiples valuation driven by Atlas A15 and A16, an LBO model with a debt schedule and returns waterfall, a merger model with accretion/dilution and synergy sensitivity, and an investment-committee memo with a recommendation, defended against a hostile Q&A rubric.

modules.title: Time Value & Capital Budgeting
modules.core: NPV, IRR and its pitfalls, payback, project cash flows, inflation and real vs. nominal, what CFOs actually do.
sources: Brealey, Myers & Allen, Principles of Corporate Finance, 14th ed. (2023)

project.title: Capital-budgeting engine
project.brief: Build a project-evaluation tool with tax, depreciation, working capital and real-vs-nominal handling, plus Monte Carlo NPV.
project.deliverable: Tested module plus a case memo.

modules.title: Cost of Capital & Capital Structure
modules.core: WACC and its estimation error, Modigliani–Miller, tax shields, trade-off vs. pecking order, market timing, leverage dynamics.
modules.lab: MM with taxes and distress costs: the optimal-leverage curve.

project.title: Cost-of-capital estimation under uncertainty
project.brief: Estimate one firm's WACC with full error propagation (beta, ERP, spreads), and show the valuation range the error implies.

modules.title: Payout, Governance & Agency
modules.core: Dividends vs. buybacks, payout irrelevance and its failures, agency costs, free cash flow, boards, executive compensation, shareholder rights.

project.title: Governance scorecard
project.brief: Score ten firms on governance from proxy-statement data, and test (with honest power caveats) whether the score relates to valuation.

modules.title: Valuation
modules.core: DCF (FCFF / FCFE), terminal value, multiples, residual income, sum of the parts, real options, and the valuation errors that dominate in practice.
modules.lab: Terminal-value share of DCF value across growth assumptions.

project.title: Atlas A16: valuation engine
project.brief: Add DCF, residual-income and multiples valuation to Atlas, driven by A15 fundamentals, with scenario and sensitivity grids.

modules.title: M&A, LBOs & Restructuring
modules.core: Takeover theory, announcement returns, synergies and overpayment, LBO mechanics and value creation, bankruptcy and Chapter 11.
sources: Grossman & Hart (1980), Bell Journal of Economics 11(1)
Andrade, Mitchell & Stafford (2001), Journal of Economic Perspectives 15(2)
Kaplan & Strömberg (2009), Journal of Economic Perspectives 23(1)
modules.lab: LBO returns decomposition: leverage vs. multiple vs. operations.

project.title: LBO model
project.brief: Build a full LBO model (sources and uses, debt tranches, cash sweep, covenants, exit) with IRR/MOIC attribution, and test it for internal consistency.

modules.title: Raising Capital & Investment Banking
modules.core: IPO underpricing, long-run IPO performance, SEOs, debt issuance, bookbuilding, underwriting economics.
sources: Ljungqvist (2007), 'IPO Underpricing', Handbook of Corporate Finance, Vol. 1

project.title: IPO pricing case
project.brief: Price a hypothetical IPO from comparables and DCF, design the book-building allocation, and explain the expected first-day return.

studio.title: Bank Stress Test: SVB Reconstruction
studio.brief: Using public FFIEC call-report data, reconstruct a failed bank's balance sheet, mark its securities to market through the 2022 rate shock, model uninsured-deposit run dynamics, and identify the decision points where the failure was preventable.

modules.title: Banking & Asset-Liability Management

modules.debate: Does private equity outperform public markets after fees?

modules.title: Venture Capital
modules.core: Staged financing, contract terms, power-law returns, selection bias in VC return data.
sources: Gompers & Lerner, The Venture Capital Cycle, 2nd ed. (2004)
modules.lab: Power-law portfolio outcomes vs. fund size.

project.title: Term-sheet economics
project.brief: Model a cap table through three rounds with liquidation preferences, anti-dilution and option pools, and compute payoffs by exit value.

modules.title: Private Credit & Infrastructure
modules.core: Direct lending, BDCs, unitranche structures, infrastructure cash flows, smoothing and marking. Thin evidence base, graded strictly.
sources: Registry seeded in Phase 0 by literature search; grades capped at C until replicated evidence is verified

project.title: Unsmoothing private credit
project.brief: Unsmooth a reported private-credit return series, and compare its true risk with a public leveraged-loan proxy.

modules.title: Real Estate Finance & Mortgage-Backed Securities
modules.core: Mortgage math, prepayment and negative convexity, agency MBS, REITs and cap rates, the housing boom and bust.

project.title: MBS pricer
project.brief: Price an agency pass-through by Monte Carlo with a rate-driven prepayment model, and compute OAS, effective duration and convexity.

studio.title: Macro Fund Simulation
studio.brief: Run a paper macro fund through a sealed set of historical episodes revealed one period at a time, using only Atlas data available at each date: regime read (A18), trade construction (A20), sizing (PR3), risk (A12). Then write the post-mortem: decisions vs. outcomes, separating skill from luck.

modules.title: Macro Data & Nowcasting
modules.core: Real-time data, revisions, dynamic factor models, nowcasting, surprise indices.
modules.lab: Revised-data lookahead bias in a backtest.

project.title: Atlas A18: nowcasting and regime dashboard
project.brief: Add a real-time-vintage dynamic-factor nowcast, a regime classifier and a cross-asset monitor to Atlas.

modules.title: Regimes & the Business Cycle
modules.core: Recession dating and prediction, the yield-curve signal, Markov switching, stock–bond correlation regimes, inflation regimes and asset returns.
sources: Campbell, Sunderam & Viceira (2017), Critical Finance Review 6(2)
Neville et al., strategies for inflationary times [WP][V]

project.title: Regime-conditional asset returns
project.brief: Classify historical regimes in real time (no look-ahead), and estimate asset-class returns by regime with honest small-sample inference.

modules.title: Trading Monetary Policy
modules.core: FOMC event studies, the pre-FOMC drift, information effects, policy divergence and FX.

project.title: Pre-FOMC drift: out-of-sample check
project.brief: Re-test the pre-FOMC drift on post-publication data, and report whether it survived.

modules.title: Macro Strategy Construction
modules.core: Expressing a view (curve trades, relative value, options vs. delta-one), carry and roll-down, convexity of expression, sizing, risk-reward asymmetry.

project.title: Atlas A20: macro trade-construction engine
project.brief: Add view → expression → sizing → scenario P&L to Atlas, reusing A5, A6, A11 and A12.

modules.title: Crises as Mechanisms
modules.core: 1992 ERM, 1997 Asia, 1998 LTCM/Russia, 2008, the 2010–12 euro crisis, the 2013 taper tantrum, the 2015 CHF de-peg, March 2020, 2022 gilts/LDI, 2023 SVB, the 2024 yen-carry unwind. Each is taught as a causal mechanism from primary sources.
sources: Primary official reports per episode (BIS, Bank of England, Federal Reserve, SNB, President's Working Group) [V]

project.title: Crisis mechanism dossier
project.brief: For two episodes, build a mechanism map (leverage, funding, forced sellers, policy response) from primary documents, plus a simulator reproducing the core dynamic.

studio.title: Financial Stability Report
studio.brief: Write a central-bank-style Financial Stability Report section using Atlas A19 outputs. Identify the three largest current vulnerabilities from public data, with mechanisms, metrics and a prioritized policy recommendation.

modules.title: Runs, Liquidity & Fire Sales
modules.core: Bank runs, liquidity spirals, fire sales, the run on repo.
sources: Shleifer & Vishny (2011), Journal of Economic Perspectives 25(1)

project.title: Run dynamics model
project.brief: Extend Diamond–Dybvig with uninsured-depositor information, and calibrate the run threshold to the 2023 regional-bank episode.

modules.title: Leverage Cycles
modules.core: Endogenous leverage, procyclical balance sheets, macro models with a financial sector.
sources: Adrian & Shin (2010), Journal of Financial Intermediation 19(3)

project.title: Leverage-cycle model
project.brief: Solve a two-period Geanakoplos collateral-equilibrium model, and show how margin shocks drive price crashes.

modules.title: Measuring Systemic Risk
modules.core: CoVaR, SRISK, MES, network contagion.

project.title: Atlas A19: systemic-risk monitor
project.brief: Add CoVaR, SRISK and MES on open data, with alert thresholds, to Atlas.

modules.title: Regulation's Market Footprint
modules.core: Basel III, the SLR, Volcker, central clearing, dealer constraints and Treasury-market liquidity, post-2020 market reform.
sources: Duffie (2020), 'Still the World's Safe Haven?', Hutchins Center Working Paper 62 [V]
Basel Committee and SEC rule texts (primary)

project.title: Regulatory-impact analysis
project.brief: Quantify how one rule (e.g., SLR treatment of Treasuries) changes dealer intermediation capacity, and evaluate the proposed reform.

studio.title: Case File from Primary Documents
studio.brief: Reconstruct one historical crisis or one enforcement case (e.g., a manipulation or insider-trading prosecution) entirely from primary documents (statutes, court opinions, official reports, contemporaneous data), with a timeline, mechanism and lessons, every assertion cited.

modules.title: Financial History
modules.core: Bubbles and panics from the Dutch Republic to 2008, the gold standard and the Great Depression, Bretton Woods and its end, the history of central banking.
sources: Kindleberger & Aliber, Manias, Panics, and Crashes, 7th ed. (2015)
Friedman & Schwartz, A Monetary History of the United States, 1867–1960 (1963)
modules.lab: Gold-standard adherence vs. depression depth on embedded data.

project.title: Then vs. now
project.brief: Pick one historical episode and one current market condition, and write a mechanism-level comparison that says where the analogy holds and where it breaks.

modules.title: Securities Law, Regulation & Professional Conduct
modules.core: The 1933 and 1934 Acts, insider-trading doctrine, manipulation, disclosure, Dodd-Frank, MiFID II, fiduciary duty, conflicts of interest, model-risk governance.
sources: Securities Act of 1933; Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (primary)
SEC v. Texas Gulf Sulphur Co., 401 F.2d 833 (2d Cir. 1968)
Federal Reserve SR 11-7, Guidance on Model Risk Management (2011) (primary)
CFA Institute Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct (practitioner)
modules.lab: Insider-trading fact-pattern classifier (rule-based, with doctrine citations).

project.title: Model-risk validation report
project.brief: Write an SR 11-7-style validation report on one of your own Atlas models: conceptual soundness, outcomes analysis, limitations, ongoing monitoring.

studio.title: Investment Committee Defense
studio.brief: Present one finished research result or trade idea to a hostile investment committee. Questions are drawn from a bank of attack angles (data, inference, costs, regime, capacity, crowding). Graded on the rubric, with recorded self-review against exemplars.

modules.title: Research Writing & Presentation
modules.core: Writing a finance paper (structure, introductions that state the result, tables that stand alone), slides, presenting to an expert audience.

project.title: Rewrite a weak paper introduction
project.brief: Rewrite three supplied weak introductions to the Cochrane standard, and annotate every change.

modules.title: Investment Memos & Trade Pitches
modules.core: The investment memo, the one-page trade pitch, base/bull/bear cases, catalysts, pre-mortems, risk and sizing sections, and how ICs actually attack.
sources: Klein (2007), 'Performing a Project Premortem', Harvard Business Review 85(9)

project.title: Two pitches
project.brief: Write one long equity pitch (from your A16 valuation) and one macro trade pitch (from your A20 engine), each surviving a scripted adversarial Q&A.

modules.title: Quant & Finance Interviews
modules.core: Probability puzzles, expected-value and market-making games, mental math, coding under time pressure, technical finance questions, case interviews.
sources: Zhou, A Practical Guide to Quantitative Finance Interviews (2008)
modules.lab: Timed probability drill set with spaced repetition.

project.title: Market-making game
project.brief: Play the in-page market-making game against scripted counterparties with hidden information, and write a post-game analysis of your edge and inventory risk.

modules.title: Reading, Refereeing & Replicating
modules.core: The referee report as a genre, full replication of a published result from open data, and diagnosing why replications diverge.
sources: Berk, Harvey & Hirshleifer (2017), 'How to Write an Effective Referee Report and Improve the Scientific Review Process', Journal of Economic Perspectives 31(1)
modules.lab: Replication-diff tool: where does my number diverge from the paper?

project.title: Replication package
project.brief: Fully replicate one assigned paper's main table from open data, document every divergence, and write a referee report on the original.

modules.title: The Great Debates
modules.core: Twelve resolutions, each with a steelman for both sides, graded evidence and a 'what would settle it' section: markets are efficient; the equity premium is a risk premium; value is dead; most factors are false discoveries; QE works via portfolio balance; UIP failure is a risk premium; complexity helps prediction; trend survived 2009; vol-managed portfolios win after costs; r* has fallen permanently; FTPL explains 2021–23; HFT improves market quality.
sources: All debate-tagged module sources; freshness pass for 2025–2026 work

project.title: Debate tournament
project.brief: For four drawn resolutions, write both sides blind, then argue the side assigned at random against the program's model brief, scored on the rubric.

modules.title: Qualifying Examination
modules.core: Timed written exams in asset pricing, econometrics and macro/monetary, modeled on PhD prelims, with full solutions released after submission.
sources: Program question bank (verified against module sources)
modules.lab: Two timed mock exams per field.

project.title: Qualifying exam
project.brief: Sit three timed exams. Pass mark per field is set by the rubric; one retake per field after a mandatory review cycle.

modules.title: Research Thesis & Defense
modules.core: Original research: question selection, pre-registration, the full Atlas pipeline, writing, presenting, defending.
sources: Discipline-specific, selected by the student and verified through the registry

project.title: Thesis
project.brief: An original, pre-registered contribution extending a replicated result, delivered as a journal-format paper with a full replication package and defended orally against the rubric.
